newsitem.title: USA: US FDA in talks with juice industry over bacteria.
newsitem.headline: US FDA in talks with juice industry over bacteria.

text.p: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) said Friday it was concerned about an outbreak of bacterial poisoning linked to fresh fruit juice and was in discussions with industry officials about how to deal with the problem.
Arthur Whitmore, a spokesman for the FDA's Center for Food Safety and Applied Nutrition in Washington, said the discussions could lead to new guidelines for the handling of fresh fruit juices.

Health officials said at least 20 cases of the bacterial infection E. coli in Washington state, California, Colorado and Canada may be linked to unpasteurized apple juice made by Odwalla Inc, a California company.
Whitmore said the outbreak was "a new type of problem."

"This is the first big producer shipping to many states where this sort of problem has come up. It does give us concern, and we are discussing with the industry how to approach the problem," he told Reuters.
He said discussions with representatives of the juice industry had begun as a result of the E. coli outbreak. The talks, which were ongoing, could lead to new guidelines, Whitmore said.
It was too soon to say whether the FDA could order fresh juice producers to pasteurize their product.
Technically, the FDA could make such an order if it was determined to be appropriate, but other options were being discussed, Whitmore said.
Odwalla prides itself on the freshness of its juices which contain no preservatives and are not pasteurized.
The FDA's investigation into the source of the outbreak continued Friday, and no conclusions had been reached, Whitmore said.
FDA investigators visited Odwalla's California plant and took samples that were being analyzed, he said.
